research_question: Given measured strong semantic readability and writable output axes but weak context-invariant dynamic codebook binding, should Trigger-2 train an addressable episode-local routing computation rather than another static semantic direction?

evidence_basis.semantic_readability_summary: approximately 0.94-1.00 from about layer 6 onward on the measured family
evidence_basis.current_interpretation: semantic state is readable and carrier/output axes are usable, but context-dependent episode-local binding/routing is not established

external_primary_research_delta.source: Wu, Geiger, Milliere, How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?, arXiv:2505.20896
external_primary_research_delta.training_implication: factor referential depth and include irrelevant binding chains/distractors; evaluate systematic dereference rather than direct lookup only

external_primary_research_delta.source: Li, Li, Huang, Steering Vector Fields for Context-Aware Inference-Time Control in Large Language Models, arXiv:2602.01654
external_primary_research_delta.training_implication: do not treat one static context-independent steering direction as sufficient when the useful direction varies by context
